sections.h2: Where is a Butler County deed filed?
sections.html:
Butler County deeds are recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office in the Government Center, Floor L, 124 West Diamond Street, Butler, PA 16001. The mailing address is P.O. Box 1208, Butler, PA 16003, and the office phone is 724-284-5340. Online, the county runs a deed search and a fee schedule on its Recorder of Deeds pages.

The county also posts a cover date that shows how far recordings have been verified. When that date trails the day you recorded, an index search will not yet show your deed, so check it before telling a buyer the record is clean. Plan books for subdivisions are posted online starting at Plan Book 315, page 27.

sections.h2: What are the Butler County recording fees?
sections.html:
The base fee for a deed, a mortgage or a re-recorded deed is $87.75 for four names, four pages and one parcel, a rate that began on November 19, 2025. Extras are small: $1 for each name beyond four, $2 for each page beyond four and $0.50 for each parcel beyond the first.

Notations beyond the first cost $2 each on mortgage documents. A land contract or article of agreement must carry a Certificate of Residence. Notary commissions and bonds cost $33.50 and are taken in cash, money order or a business check only.

sections.h2: What does Butler County charge to copy records?
sections.html:
Mail requests for record books or instrument numbers cost $1 per page, while a certificate and seal of office is $1.50. A service fee of $2 applies per document when you supply the book and page, and $4 per document when you do not. Plan book copies by mail run $2 per page, and an Act 287 search costs $2 per township.

  • Maps and plans: $45 covers page one, then $40 for each page after.
  • Highway plans: $15 covers page one, then $3 for every page after.
  • GRID setup: $7 per name.

These charges matter to sellers who need a copy of an old easement or plat for a title company. Order by instrument number when you can, since the lower service fee applies when the book and page are known.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies when a Butler County house sells?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania imposes a 1% state realty transfer tax on the value of real estate transferred by deed, and the county recorder collects any local tax with it. State revenue officials hold the grantor and grantee jointly liable for the tax. Ask the Butler County Recorder of Deeds for the total rate that applies to your municipality and school district before you price the sale.

Some transfers escape the tax, such as certain family conveyances, transfers to government units, and property passed by will or intestacy. A deed that reflects one of those exemptions needs the state's Statement of Value to explain it. The county also posts a Common Level Ratio Factor for each July 1 to June 30 period. Its page lists the earlier factor of 16.67 for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.

sections.h2: How do Butler County tax sales touch a seller?
sections.html:
The Tax Claim Bureau runs an Upset Sale on the second Monday of September for properties two years behind on taxes. A buyer at that sale takes on past due taxes, liens and mortgages. Properties that fail to sell move to a Judicial Sale, where bidding starts at costs plus deed recording and transfer fees and the property is sold free and clear if all parties were properly notified.

Anything still unsold goes to the Repository List. A bidder there fills out a bid form, and the Bureau presents the highest bid to the three taxing districts for approval.

The Bureau is at 124 West Diamond Street, with a mailing address at P.O. Box 1208, and its phone is 724-284-5326. It is open Monday through Friday, opening at half past eight and closing at 4 p.m. An owner behind on taxes should call there before the September sale.

sections.h2: Which place name goes on a Butler County deed?
sections.html:
Use the legal municipality, which is often a township, and not the mailing-address village. Butler is the only city in the county. Communities such as Renfrew, Lyndora, Herman, Sarver, Cabot, Boyers and Forestville have their own post offices and zip codes but lie entirely inside townships, so a deed that names the village instead of the township can point the recorder, the assessor and the school district at the wrong place.

  • Take the municipality and school district from the latest tax bill, not from a listing.
  • Match every owner name to the prior deed, since names over four add $1 each.
  • Count pages before you sign, because each page past four adds $2.

Eight counties touch Butler County, among them Allegheny, Armstrong, Lawrence and Venango. A parcel near a boundary belongs to one county only, so confirm the county of record before you send a package.

sections.h2: What should Butler County homeowners know about the area?
sections.html:
Butler County covers 795 square miles north of Pittsburgh, was created from Allegheny County on March 12, 1800, and is named for Revolutionary War General Richard Butler. The city of Butler is the seat, and Cranberry Township is the largest township. The 2020 census counted 193,763 residents, and an estimate for 2025 stands at 200,169.

History here includes John Roebling's wire rope works at Saxonburg and the Jeep, which American Bantam developed in the county in 1941. Moraine State Park, with its 3,000-acre Lake Arthur, draws weekend traffic. The Allegheny River touches the northeast and southeast corners, and the county's climate is humid continental, with July averages near 72 degrees in the borough of Butler.

Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a median value of $294,200 for owner-occupied homes, median household income of $89,843 and a 76.9% owner rate. The county issued 1,246 building permits in 2025. Public school districts include Butler Area, Seneca Valley, Mars Area, Knoch, Moniteau and Slippery Rock Area, among others. Main roads are I-79, I-76, I-80, US 19 and US 422.

faqs.q: What is the base fee to record a deed in Butler County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $87.75 for a deed, mortgage or re-recorded deed that has four names, four pages and one parcel. Names over four cost $1 each, pages over four cost $2 each and extra parcels cost $0.50 each. The fee started on November 19, 2025.

faqs.q: Where is the Butler County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in the Government Center, Floor L, at 124 West Diamond Street in Butler. Phone 724-284-5340. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1208, Butler, PA 16003.

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate of Residence in Butler County?
faqs.a: Yes for an article of agreement or an installment land contract, which the county says must carry one. The base fee for either document is $59.75 for four pages. Pages over four are $2 each and names over four are $1 each.

faqs.q: Who collects transfer tax on a Butler County sale?
faqs.a: The county Recorder of Deeds collects it at recording. The state rate is 1% of the value, and local taxes can add to that. Ask the office for the rate for your municipality and school district.

faqs.q: When is the Butler County upset tax sale?
faqs.a: The Upset Sale is held on the second Monday of each September. It covers properties that are two years delinquent. Unsold properties move to a Judicial Sale and then to the Repository List.
